title: Uber — Calendar Application Rehearsal
briefing: An Uber L4 candidate reported calendar system design alongside React coding exercises and described difficulty keeping the discussion focused. The frontend scope below is a Codematica adaptation. Design a calendar with month/week views, event creation, editing, and recurring meetings. This exercise adapts a public candidate report; company attribution and interview details are not independently verified. The practice constraints and follow-ups are Codematica additions. Use your own timer and drawing tool: 45 minutes designing, 10 minutes handling follow-ups, and 5 minutes reviewing. No coding is required. Your design is not automatically graded; reflection text is transient. The related lesson contains the source and shared rubric.
objectives: Define event identity, time zone, recurrence rules, exceptions, and the visible date range.
Draw the calendar shell, date navigation, event layout, editor, and range-based data fetching.
Separate stored event semantics from display formatting. Explain overlapping-event layout, cache updates, and keyboard navigation.

prediction.prompt: Which area is most likely to expose a weakness in your first design?

options.label: An uncertain request outcome or recovery gap.
Performance or accessibility under the stated constraints.

steps.title: 0–7 minutes: clarify the scope
steps.instructions: Design a calendar with month/week views, event creation, editing, and recurring meetings. Identify two main journeys, required devices, freshness, permissions, and exclusions. Separate requirements from assumptions.

steps.title: 7–20 minutes: draw the architecture
steps.instructions: Draw the calendar shell, date navigation, event layout, editor, and range-based data fetching. Assign state owners and component inputs/events. Include loading, empty, and error states.

steps.title: 20–30 minutes: define data and APIs
steps.instructions: Define event identity, time zone, recurrence rules, exceptions, and the visible date range. Specify one read and one write, including identities, response fields, cache policy, and safe retry conditions.

steps.title: 30–45 minutes: trace behavior and recovery
steps.instructions: Trace one interaction from input to confirmed state, then fail a request. Separate stored event semantics from display formatting. Explain overlapping-event layout, cache updates, and keyboard navigation.

steps.title: 45–55 minutes: handle follow-ups
steps.instructions: Edit one occurrence versus the series. Change time zones. Cross a daylight-saving transition. Resolve two users editing the same event. Pick the hardest case and show which decisions change. State any unresolved limits.

steps.title: 55–60 minutes: review your evidence
steps.instructions: Score scope, components, state and data, APIs and consistency, failure recovery, and quality and trade-offs. Use 0: missing, 1: mentioned, 2: explained with a concrete decision and consequence. Check only evidence you can show. Choose the weakest dimension and redraw it; this is not an employer hiring threshold.

evidenceChecklist.label: I stated the main journeys, assumptions, and exclusions.
I drew component responsibilities and interaction contracts.
I assigned state owners, stable identities, and invariants.
I defined reads, writes, caching, and reconciliation.
I traced one failure through usable recovery.
I defended accessibility, performance, measurement, and alternatives.
I distinguished recurring series from occurrences and traced a time-zone or concurrent-edit case.

reflectionPrompts: Separate stored event semantics from display formatting. Explain overlapping-event layout, cache updates, and keyboard navigation.
Which decision changed after a follow-up, and what requirement caused it?
Which dimension was weakest, and what will you redraw next time?
extensionChallenge: Move one occurrence of a recurring meeting across a daylight-saving transition while another user edits the series. Define the conflict policy and what each participant sees.
